rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidates: chunk 6 line 47 "The agent's first read was partly wrong" and chunk 7 line 61 "The file you wrote today is the smallest unit that qualifies" — both definite references to the student's own just-completed exercise artifacts (the bug/fix from fix-tests-first, the CLAUDE.local.md file from compound-and-close). This lecture is M1's closer placed directly after all four M1 exercises (confirmed via curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/getting-going.md include order: orient-and-introspect → fix-tests-first → close-the-ticket → compound-and-close), so the module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out applies throughout: the referent is the student's lived module, not a missing slide. "the opening lecture's mirror" (chunk 1 line 10) is a term this file defines in the same sentence and then reuses at chunk 5 ("The mirror is steered by...") — same-file reuse, not-a-violation per the rule's own example. No pronoun/demonstrative anywhere lacks an in-chunk, in-file, or carve-out-backed antecedent.

chunk 1 line 10: "This is the machinery under the opening lecture's mirror: the LLM that flatters you, calls unfinished work progress, mirrors your stance." Names the source by its claim, fully unpacked in the same sentence — structurally matches this rule's own PASS exemplar ("the opening lecture's infinite chameleon: the LLM that flatters you…"). No bare positional pointer ("The opening lecture said…") appears anywhere in the file. No other cross-file callback found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 6 line 44/47 "Orient, fix, close, compound. You just ran that loop." maps 1:1 to the four M1 exercise files, confirmed live: `ls curriculum/exercises/` returns orient-and-introspect.md, fix-tests-first.md, close-the-ticket.md, compound-and-close.md. chunk 7 line 61 "The file you wrote today" resolves to compound-and-close.md's CLAUDE.local.md deliverable, confirmed by this file's own maintainer block: "The file is owned by compound-and-close (which writes it)." All backward references resolve to beats that exist in the module's current exercise set.

All 7 chunks carry 3-4 substantive bullets or a full paragraph with an independent claim. Thinnest case: chunk 6 (one paragraph, no bullets) still self-carries — names the loop, describes what happened in it, attributes the coined term — not a wait-state or context-dependent fragment.

Every header is a true summary of its chunk under the sequential read, e.g. chunk 4 header "The LLM answers in essays" against its own line 31 "The fix was small; the answers around it were pages" — direct match. No header is contradicted by its chunk's body.

Checked all sub-items across all 7 chunks. (i) "Not X. Not Y. Z." — grep -nE '\bNot [A-Za-z].*\.\s*Not [A-Za-z]' on the body → 0 hits. (ii) anaphora/epistrophe triple — closest candidate chunk 5 lines 38-40 ("The mirror is steered by what you bring… is steered by what you build… is steered by what you ask for") is a parallel construction, not a repeated-phrase tic, and each of its three legs carries genuinely distinct concrete content (posture/tests/output-shape, each tied back to chunks 1/3/4) — clears the rule's own "third leg carries new content" test even scored as a triple. (iii) self-grading superlative — grep -niE 'one of the (most|best)|most (useful|important|powerful|valuable)|best (way|tool|move)' → 0 hits. (iv) number+retraction — chunk 3 line 24 "nine times in ten… seven-step chain… The numbers are an illustration, not a measurement" IS the shape, but this file's own maintainer block (line 85, "Laws carried") explicitly attests it deliberate: "a worded subjunctive illustration… Zombie-stat guard: do NOT let edits promote it to a measured constant" — matches the rule's own EXCEPT clause. (v) abstraction-noun stacks — none found; language stays concrete (the agent's report, the failing test, the code). (vi) verb triplets with an empty leg — none found.
